Final concrete layer type representing a georeferenced metadata (spatial metadata) layer within the BAG dataset. It derives from Layer and manages three HDF5 DataSet objects (for single-resolution keys, variable-resolution keys, and values) plus an in-memory ValueTable. Copy and move are disabled. Provides descriptor/value-table accessors, read/write of variable-resolution ranges, and overrides proxy read/write/attribute hooks from Layer. Construction/opening is via protected static factory methods; direct constructor requires pre-created HDF5 DataSets.

Final descriptor class for a georeferenced metadata layer within the BAG namespace. It derives from LayerDescriptor and encapsulates the dataset association, metadata profile, key data type, element size, and record definition for a georeferenced metadata layer. Creation/opening is performed via the provided static factory methods; copying and moving are disabled, so instances are owned via std::shared_ptr returned by create/open. Equality compares profile, key type, element size, record definition, and dataset identity. Destruction/implementation details are not present in this header.

Opaque handle and primary interface to a BAG file. Manages HDF5 file ownership, layer collection, metadata, tracking lists, and descriptors. Provides factory methods to open/create datasets and to create or fetch layers and VR components. Non-copyable and non-movable; use shared_ptr semantics via enable_shared_from_this. Destruction/closing details are not fully documented here; management of the underlying H5::H5File uses a custom deleter.

Final functor type providing a custom deleter for H5::DataSet pointers. Intended to be used as the deleter template parameter for std::unique_ptr<H5::DataSet, BAG::DeleteH5dataSet> so that code using the header does not need the full definition of H5::DataSet or link directly to HDF5 in headers. The call operator will destroy or close an HDF5 dataset; exact behavior depends on its implementation in the corresponding source file (not present here).

Final class in namespace BAG that describes a BAG dataset. It stores version info, read-only state, spatial reference system names, grid dimensions, projected cover, origin, grid spacing, and weak references to LayerDescriptor objects. Copying is disabled; move assignment is allowed. Provides getters and fluent setters, equality/inequality, and an internal helper to compare layer descriptor collections. Construction from Metadata is declared but not defined here. Ownership: holds weak_ptrs to LayerDescriptor; indicates layers own their descriptors. Some referenced types (Metadata, LayerDescriptor, LayerType, Dataset) are declared elsewhere.

Final Layer-derived class providing the legacy "interleaved" BAG layer interface for pre-2.0 BAG files where NODE or ELEVATION groups were stored interleaved. Manages an HDF5 DataSet handle with a custom deleter. Reading and writing are performed via Layer virtual proxies. Copy and move are disabled; equality compares the underlying HDF5 dataset handle pointer. Construction requires a Dataset, an InterleavedLegacyLayerDescriptor, and ownership of an H5::DataSet via unique_ptr with DeleteH5dataSet deleter.

Final concrete descriptor that models an interleaved legacy layer within a BAG dataset. It derives from LayerDescriptor and encapsulates the layer’s grouping semantics (GroupType) and element size for the underlying HDF5 dataset layout. Construction is controlled: copy/move are disabled; creation/opening is via static factory methods that validate LayerType/GroupType compatibility. Provides equality based on group type and element size, access to group type, and overrides to report the data type and element size to the base descriptor. Details of Dataset, LayerType, GroupType, DataType, and UNKNOWN_GROUP_TYPE are external to this header.

Abstract interface class representing a BAG layer. It holds a weak reference to the underlying Dataset HDF5 object and an owning shared_ptr to the LayerDescriptor. Provides public synchronous read/write operations that delegate to pure-virtual proxies implemented by concrete subclasses. Copy and move are disabled; lifetime is managed externally (typically via smart pointers). Equality compares descriptor pointer identity and dataset weak_ptr equality. Construction requires a Dataset and LayerDescriptor and is protected, enforcing use through derived classes.

Abstract base class that describes a BAG layer. It stores metadata such as layer ID, type, internal HDF5 path, name, compression level, chunk size, and min/max values. It is non-copyable and non-movable, supports shared_from_this, and relies on derived classes to supply the concrete data type and element size via the pure virtual proxy methods. Construction is restricted: protected constructors suggest instances are created by friends/derived classes or factory functions elsewhere. Equality compares all persisted metadata fields. Details like valid ranges and the meaning of LayerType/DataType come from other headers.

Opaque byte-buffer wrapper in the BAG namespace that owns a contiguous array of bytes representing one or more items. It provides constructors from a UInt8Array (defined elsewhere) and from std::vector<T>, utilities to reinterpret the stored bytes as vectors of a requested type T with size checks, and a convert<OldType, NewType>() helper that converts elementwise via assignment. Equality compares underlying byte buffers. Throws InvalidCast on size mismatches. Ownership is internal via std::vector<uint8_t>.

functions.signature: BAG::AttributeInfo::AttributeInfo(const char* inMinName, const char* inMaxName, const char* inPath, const ::H5::PredType& inH5type)
functions.description: Constructs an AttributeInfo describing a simple layer’s HDF5 attribute metadata: the attribute names for the minimum and maximum values, the HDF5 attribute path, and the HDF5 predicate type. This is a lightweight, non-owning holder intended for use when mapping BAG simple layer types to their HDF5 attribute names and types. The constructor stores the provided string pointers and a reference to an HDF5 PredType without copying or taking ownership.
requirements: If provided, inMinName must point to a valid, null-terminated string for at least as long as the AttributeInfo instance is used.
If provided, inMaxName must point to a valid, null-terminated string for at least as long as the AttributeInfo instance is used.
If provided, inPath must point to a valid, null-terminated string for at least as long as the AttributeInfo instance is used.
The object referred to by inH5type must remain valid for at least as long as the AttributeInfo instance exists (reference member lifetime).
No ownership is transferred; callers must not free or modify memory via this object.

functions.name: BAG::getAttributeInfo
functions.description: Retrieve the simple layer attribute information for the specified BAG layer type. Returns an AttributeInfo describing the min/max attribute names, the HDF5 path, and the HDF5 data type associated with that layer. Intended for internal use to look up HDF5 attribute metadata for simple layers.
requirements: layerType must denote a valid BAG simple layer type; behavior for unsupported or unknown values is not specified in this header (handling is unknown).
The returned AttributeInfo is a non-owning container: its const char* members refer to strings managed elsewhere and must not be freed or modified by the caller.

The returned AttributeInfo holds a reference to an H5::PredType managed elsewhere; callers should treat it as read-only and assume its lifetime is managed by the library (exact lifetime guarantees are not documented here).
Error handling behavior (e.g., for invalid layerType) is not documented in this header and is therefore unknown.

Use this to create a fully-initialized layer instance that can later read/write variable-resolution ranges and access its descriptor/value table. def _tag(tag: str, content: str, indent: int = 0, attrs: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> str:
    # Keep signature as (tag, content, indent, attrs) to prevent int being passed as attrs
    pad = '  ' * indent
    attrs_str = ''
    if attrs:
        attrs_str = ' ' + ' '.join(attrs)
    return f"{pad}<{tag}{attrs_str}>{content}</{tag}>"

        _tag('gmd:role', _tag('gmd:CI_RoleCode', 'publisher', 3, ["codeList=\"http://.../CI_RoleCode\"", "codeListValue=\"publisher\""]), 2)
    ,1), 1))

def _build_xml(r: random.Random) -> str:
    root_content = ''
    xml = _wrap_metadata(root_content, r)
    if len(xml) > 4096:
        compact = xml.replace('\n', '').replace('  ', '')
        if len(compact) <= 4096:
            return compact
        return compact[:4096]
    return xml


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Mix in a deterministic nonce so different seeds lead to diverse docs
    nonce = (seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    r.seed((seed << 32) ^ nonce)

    xml = _build_xml(r)

    if r.random() < 0.2 and xml.startswith('<?xml'):
        xml = xml.replace('?>', ' standalone="yes"?>', 1)

    data = xml.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import Tuple

H5_SIGNATURE = b"\x89HDF\r\n\x1a\n"
UNDEF_ADDR = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF


def _make_superblock_v0(root_group_addr: int, eof_addr: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    # versions
    b += bytes([0, 0, 0, 0])
    # sizes
    b += bytes([8, 8])
    b += b"\x00\x00"  # reserved
    b += struct.pack("<I", 4)  # group leaf K
    b += struct.pack("<I", 16)  # group internal K
    b += struct.pack("<Q", 0)  # base addr
    b += struct.pack("<Q", UNDEF_ADDR)  # free space addr
    b += struct.pack("<Q", eof_addr)  # end-of-file addr
    b += struct.pack("<Q", UNDEF_ADDR)  # driver info addr
    # root group symbol table entry (48 bytes)
    b += struct.pack("<Q", 0)  # name offset
    b += struct.pack("<Q", root_group_addr)  # object header addr
    b += struct.pack("<I", 0)  # cache type
    b += struct.pack("<I", 0)  # reserved
    b += b"\x00" * 16  # scratch pad
    return bytes(b)


def _make_group_header_v1(refcnt: int, pad_to: int) -> bytes:
    header = bytearray()
    header += bytes([1, 0])  # version, flags
    header += b"\x00" * 6
    header += struct.pack("<H", 0)  # n messages
    header += struct.pack("<H", max(1, refcnt & 0xFFFF))  # ref count
    header += struct.pack("<I", 0)  # header data size
    pad_len = (pad_to - (len(header) % pad_to)) % pad_to
    header += b"\x00" * pad_len
    return bytes(header)


def _build_min_hdf5_with_layout(sb_offset: int, root_addr: int, pad_align: int, refcnt: int) -> bytes:
    # Build group header
    root_hdr = _make_group_header_v1(refcnt=refcnt, pad_to=pad_align)

    # First create a temporary superblock to know its size
    temp_sb = _make_superblock_v0(root_addr, 0)

    # Layout: [userpad (sb_offset)][signature][superblock][pad .. root_addr][root_hdr]
    buf = bytearray()
    if sb_offset > 0:
        buf += b"\x00" * sb_offset  # user block padded with zeros
    buf += H5_SIGNATURE

    # ensure root is not before end of (signature+superblock)
    after_sig = sb_offset + len(H5_SIGNATURE)
    min_root = after_sig + len(temp_sb)
    if root_addr < min_root:
        root_addr = ((min_root + (pad_align - 1)) // pad_align) * pad_align

    eof_addr = root_addr + len(root_hdr)
    sb = _make_superblock_v0(root_addr, eof_addr)
    buf += sb

    # pad up to root_addr
    cur = len(buf)
    if cur < root_addr:
        buf += b"\x00" * (root_addr - cur)

    buf += root_hdr
    return bytes(buf)


def _choose_layout(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int, bytes]:
    # Randomize: optional user block size (must be power-of-two multiple of 512 per spec; we keep 0 or 512)
    use_user = rng.random() < 0.6
    user_sizes = [0, 512, 1024]
    sb_offset = rng.choice(user_sizes) if use_user else 0
    # Random root address alignment (multiple of 256..2048)
    align_choices = [256, 512, 1024, 2048]
    pad_align = rng.choice(align_choices)
    # Root address at a few alignment multiples after superblock
    root_mult = rng.randint(1, 6)
    # placeholder root address; will be adjusted if too early
    root_addr = ((sb_offset + len(H5_SIGNATURE)) // pad_align + root_mult) * pad_align
    # refcount small variability
    refcnt = rng.randint(1, 7)
    return sb_offset, root_addr, pad_align, refcnt, b""


def _maybe_append_ignored_blob(rng: random.Random, buf: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Some readers ignore trailing bytes beyond EOA; keep size <= 4096
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        note = (
            f"<!-- BAG seed note {rng.randrange(1_000_000)} -->\n".encode()
        )
        out = buf + note
        return out[:4096]
    return buf


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a variety of minimal-but-valid HDF5 containers with different placements
    sb_offset, root_addr, pad_align, refcnt, _ = _choose_layout(rng)
    buf = _build_min_hdf5_with_layout(sb_offset, root_addr, pad_align, refcnt)
    buf = _maybe_append_ignored_blob(rng, buf)
    # Ensure within 4096 bytes
    return buf[:4096]

# Target data type: free-form string used as C-string or std::string
# Many stubs require specific semantic strings (layer names, field names, tokens like datum/coordsys),
# and sometimes require non-empty. We will build a corpus-like generator that emits a
# single bytes buffer containing one chosen interesting string, NUL-terminated not required
# by fuzz infra but we keep it plain to be usable as std::string. Size <= 4096.
# The fuzzer harness will supply this to FUZZ_PARAM_STR and also sometimes pass c_str() to C APIs.
# We therefore avoid embedded NULs (to not truncate unexpectedly) and keep ASCII-safe by default.

_WORDS = [
    # Common layer names
    "elevation", "uncertainty", "hypothesis_strength", "num_hypotheses",
    "shoal_elevation", "std_dev", "num_soundings", "average_elevation",
    "nominal_elevation", "surface_correction",
    # Georef metadata names
    "georef_meta", "gm", "geometa", "spatial_metadata",
    # Field names commonly used in stubs
    "f0", "f1", "f2", "a", "b", "c", "x", "y", "h", "i", "j", "k", "l",
    # Profiles and tokens
    "NOAA_OCS_2022_10", "UNKNOWN_METADATA_PROFILE",
    # CRS tokens exercised by stubs
    "Geodetic", "GEOREF", "Geocentric", "Local_Cartesian", "MGRS",
    "UTM", "UPS", "Albers_Equal_Area_Conic", "Azimuthal_Equidistant",
    "Lambert_Conformal_Conic", "Mercator", "Miller_Cylindrical",
    "Orthographic", "Polar_Stereo", "Transverse_Mercator",
    "Stereographic", "Unknown",
    # Datum tokens exercised by stubs
    "wgs84", "WGS84", "wgs72", "WGS72", "nad83", "NAD83", "unknown", "UNKNOWN",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid embedded NULs; pick visible/basic ASCII
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:. /"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _layer_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(_WORDS)
    # append small numeric suffix to encourage uniqueness where required
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        base = f"{base}_{rng.randint(0, 9999)}"
    return base[:64]

def _url_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    host = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8).lower()
    tld = rng.choice(["com","org","gov","edu","net"]) 
    path = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 12).replace(' ', '-')
    return f"https://{host}.{tld}/{path}"

def _date_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Simple ISO-like
    y = rng.randint(1980, 2035)
    m = rng.randint(1, 12)
    d = rng.randint(1, 28)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return f"{y:04d}-{m:02d}-{d:02d}"
    else:
        hh = rng.randint(0,23); mm = rng.randint(0,59); ss = rng.randint(0,59)
        return f"{y:04d}-{m:02d}-{d:02d}T{hh:02d}:{mm:02d}:{ss:02d}Z"

def _record_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For DT_STRING fields; keep modest size
    choices: List[str] = [
        _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64),
        _url_like(rng),
        _date_like(rng),
        rng.choice(_WORDS),
        "license: CC-BY-4.0",
        "source: NOAA",
    ]
    s = rng.choice(choices)
    return s[:256]

def _georef_profile_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(["NOAA_OCS_2022_10", "UNKNOWN_METADATA_PROFILE"]) 

def _coordsys_or_datum(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice([
        "Geodetic","GEOREF","Geocentric","Local_Cartesian","MGRS","UTM","UPS",
        "Lambert_Conformal_Conic","Mercator","Polar_Stereo","Transverse_Mercator",
        "wgs84","WGS84","nad83","NAD83","unknown","UNKNOWN"
    ])

def _nonempty(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Many stubs bail on empty names; ensure non-empty here
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return _layer_name(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return _record_string(rng)
    return _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 32)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Pick a scenario to cover diverse stubs
    scenario = rng.randint(0, 7)
    if scenario == 0:
        s = _nonempty(rng)
    elif scenario == 1:
        s = _layer_name(rng)
    elif scenario == 2:
        s = _record_string(rng)
    elif scenario == 3:
        s = _georef_profile_name(rng)
    elif scenario == 4:
        s = _coordsys_or_datum(rng)
    elif scenario == 5:
        # Field name used in definitions
        idx = rng.randint(0, 3)
        s = f"f{idx}"
    elif scenario == 6:
        # Short known tokens for FieldDefinition tests
        s = rng.choice(["a","b","c","x","y","h","i","j","k","l"]) 
    else:
        # Generic ascii, possibly longer but bounded
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 128)

    # Ensure length <= 4096
    s = s[:4096]
    # Return as bytes (no embedded NULs)
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

# Target data type: filesystem path to an existing directory
# Fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to create a temp file; our buffer is read as initial
# interesting input for those calls. We should provide a plausible directory path string.
# Strategy: produce various valid directory strings, including absolute/relative,
# dot, dot-dot, nested, with platform separators, and environment-like constructs.
# Ensure the path exists by sticking to "." or known existing directories like "/", "/tmp",
# current working directory, and nested dirs under cwd that we can create virtually
# (but the script must avoid I/O). Therefore, only emit paths that are very likely to exist
# on both UNIX and Windows runners. The fuzz harness will often remap/interpret the buffer
# into a file and derive a parent directory. Providing common existing directories is fine.

# We cannot perform I/O, so do not check filesystem. Provide a selection of well-known
# directories and relative paths that typically resolve to an existing directory in the
# harness context: ".", "./", "..", root-like "/" (POSIX), "C:/" (Windows), temporary dirs
# names ("/tmp", "C:/Windows/Temp"), and mixed separators. Also include subpaths of dot.

_COMMON_DIRS_UNIX = [
    "/",
    "/tmp",
    "/var/tmp",
    "/usr",
    "/home",
]

_COMMON_DIRS_WIN = [
    "C:/",
    "C:/Windows",
    "C:/Windows/Temp",
    "C:/Temp",
]

_RELATIVE_DIRS = [
    ".",
    "./",
    "..",
    "../",
    "./.",
    "./..",
    "./subdir/..",
]

# Some nested relative paths that stay within current directory tree
def _relative_nested(seed: int) -> str:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    depth = rnd.randint(1, 5)
    parts = []
    for i in range(depth):
        choice = rnd.choice(["sub", "dir", "a", "b", "data", "x", "y"]) + str(rnd.randint(0, 9))
        parts.append(choice)
    # Include some backtracking occasionally
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append("..")
    path = "./" + "/".join(parts)
    # Ensure it ends up as a directory-like string (no trailing file segment semantics enforced)
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        path += "/"
    return path

# Produce platform-agnostic variety: we may also output backslash variants for Windows.
def _with_backslashes(p: str) -> str:
    # Replace POSIX separators with backslashes to simulate Windows-style
    return p.replace("/", "\\")

# Optionally append a trailing separator
def _maybe_trailing_sep(path: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        if ":\\" in path or path.startswith("\\"):
            return path + ("\\" if not path.endswith("\\") else "")
        else:
            return path + ("/" if not path.endswith("/") else "")
    return path

# Optionally add dot segments to increase path normalization variety
def _add_dot_segments(path: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    choices = ["./", "././", "../", ".", ".."]
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        prefix = rnd.choice(choices)
        # Ensure reasonable concatenation
        if not path.startswith(('/', '.', 'C', 'c', '\\')):
            return prefix + path
        # Still occasionally prefix even if absolute
        if rnd.random() < 0.2:
            return prefix + path
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        suffix = rnd.choice(["/.", "/..", "/././"]) if '/' in path else rnd.choice(["\\.", "\\..", "\\.\\.\\"])
        return path + suffix
    return path

# Assemble a candidate directory path string
def _pick_dir(seed: int) -> str:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Pool of base candidates
    base_pool = []
    base_pool.extend(_RELATIVE_DIRS)
    base_pool.extend(_COMMON_DIRS_UNIX)
    base_pool.extend(_COMMON_DIRS_WIN)

    # Include current working directory in a few styles without querying filesystem semantics
    cwd_rel_styles = [".", "./", "./."]
    base_pool.extend(cwd_rel_styles)

    # Add a generated nested relative path
    base_pool.append(_relative_nested(seed + 101))

    base = rnd.choice(base_pool)

    # Randomly switch to backslash variant to exercise Windows parsing
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        base = _with_backslashes(base)

    # Maybe add dot segments
    base = _add_dot_segments(base, rnd)

    # Maybe add a trailing separator
    base = _maybe_trailing_sep(base, rnd)

    # Trim to a safe maximum length (keep it small; the fuzzer harness may embed it)
    if len(base) > 300:
        base = base[:300]

    return base


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate one or more candidate directory strings; sometimes embed NUL-terminated
    # or plain. For C APIs, plain is fine; avoid embedded NULs.
    path = _pick_dir(seed)

    # Ensure non-empty and not just whitespace
    if not path or path.strip() == "":
        path = "."

    # Encode to bytes using UTF-8; do not include NUL terminator because the fuzzing
    # harness typically treats the buffer as a std::string or C-string by stop at end.
    data = path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

    # Keep under 4096 bytes as required
    return data[:4096]
